answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind cryptographic attestation chains via zero-knowledge proofs to a verifiable identity tree rooted in physical hardware anchors. When a rogue swarm attempts mass replication, entry staking imposes an exponential capital exhaustion penalty where each sibling identity scales costs as $C = b^n$. Like a sudden zephyr shifting an arid dune, illicit clusters collapse before reaching the fertile meadow of trusted network consensus.
